algarve.overview: The Algarve is known for its dramatic coastal hiking, led by the Seven Hanging Valleys trail that traces limestone cliffs and sea caves above the Atlantic. For multi-day routes, the Fishermen's Trail is an 11- to 13-day, 140-mile coastal trek along the rugged west, while the 186-mile Via Algarviana crosses the inland hills in 14 stages. Shade is scarce, so spring and autumn are best and summer needs a dawn start.

new-orleans.overview: Walking here means short, flat nature trails and urban parks. Couturie Forest in City Park has a mile-long path under the canopy, and the Twin Canals Trail in Barataria Preserve, part of Jean Lafitte National Historical Park, is a short out-and-back between two canals. Most of the preserve's swamp boardwalks are being rebuilt.

months.1: Mild temperatures make this a comfortable time for the Couturie Forest paths and the canal trail.
months.3: Spring warmth arrives, and the Couturie Forest trails and the canal path are pleasant before the heat builds.
months.5: Increasing heat and humidity make the unshaded marsh path less comfortable.
months.6: Brutal heat, high humidity, and heavy insect activity make the forest and canal trails oppressive.
months.7: Heat and humidity peak, and insects swarm over the trails, making walking unpleasant.
months.8: Hot, airless days leave the unshaded marsh path punishing, and even the shaded forest paths are sticky.
months.9: Heat and humidity linger, and sudden downpours can drench the trails.

southeast-alaska.overview: Hiking here means walking into deep coastal rainforests and up to glacier views, often starting right from the port towns. Juneau has the steep, unmaintained West Glacier Trail for a close look at the ice, while Skagway is the start of the historic Chilkoot gold rush trail, where the border crossing is closed, so hikers walk only the US or the Canadian side and turn back at the border. The season is short, driven by snowmelt, with trails at their best from June to August.

months.6: Summer hiking is in full swing. The Chilkoot Trail opens for permitted hikers, one side of the border only, and the West Glacier Trail is clear enough for a steep day hike, though rain is always possible.
months.7: This is the peak of the short hiking season. The Chilkoot Trail is clear of snow, and day hikers can tackle the steep, unmaintained routes to glacier views under the best chance of clear skies.

taiwan.overview: Taiwan's hiking runs from the volcanic peaks around Taipei to the high-altitude trails of the Central Mountain Range. The most well known trekking route is the demanding ascent of Yushan, a two-day trek to a 12,970-foot summit that requires a lottery permit. Day hikers can ride the forest railway to Alishan for walks among ancient cypress trees or climb the volcanic summits of Yangmingshan near Taipei. October and November bring the clearest skies and most comfortable temperatures for the trails.

months.3: Temperatures begin to warm, melting the high-elevation snow. Forest trails at Alishan and in Yangmingshan become lush and vibrant, making it a fine time for day hikes before the heavy rains arrive.
months.4: Clearer spring weather makes this a strong month for Alishan's forest trails or lower mountain loops. The high-altitude routes on Yushan begin to open for standard trekking as the last ice clears.
months.8: The threat of typhoons remains high, frequently closing the Yushan trails and other mountain paths for safety. When the weather holds, the high humidity makes any significant climbing a massive effort.
months.10: This is the best month for walking in Taiwan, with clear skies and comfortable temperatures. The views from Yushan are spectacular, and the forest and ridge trails at Alishan and Yangmingshan are in excellent condition.
